title: Grove sets AMM swap parameters by venue archetype rather than per-venue assessment, using an identical triple on different chains and different AMMs
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.2.2.1.2.4.3 sets the Avalanche Curve USDS/USDC swap rate limits to `maxAmount`: 5,000,000, `slope`: 100,000,000 per day, `maxSlippage`: 0.1%. The Ethereum Uniswap v3 AUSD/USDC Swaps Instance carries exactly the same three values. Different chain, different AMM, different token pair, identical control.

The structural echo goes further. Curve on Avalanche is split into a **Swaps** Instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.2.2.1) and an **LP** Instance (.2.2.2) that share one pool address, `0xA9d7d3D7…`, exactly as the Uniswap Instances share one Ethereum pool. In both cases the Swaps Instance records deposit and withdrawal limits as "N/A - swaps only" and an outflow RateLimitID of "N/A," while the LP Instance carries a full inflow/outflow pair.

So Grove is not configuring venues individually. It is applying a reusable **AMM archetype**: split the venue into a swaps mandate and a liquidity-provision mandate, give swaps a standard volume/slope/slippage triple, and give LP a deposit cap with unlimited withdrawal.

The benefit is consistency and reviewability — a new AMM allocation can be assessed against a known template rather than from scratch, and a deviation from the template is itself a signal worth examining. The cost is that a parameter which recurs unchanged stops being evidence of judgement. A 0.1% slippage bound that is correct for a deep Ethereum stable pair is not obviously correct for a newer pool on another chain, where thinner liquidity makes the same bound either unreachable in practice or unexpectedly binding. Template parameters need re-derivation per venue precisely because they look already-decided.
description: The Avalanche Curve USDS/USDC swap limits match the Ethereum Uniswap AUSD/USDC ones exactly — 5m maxAmount, 100m per day slope, 0.1% maxSlippage — despite different protocols, pairs and networks.
